title: Woman sentenced for Pensacola bike crash, fleeing scene - NewsBreak
text: PENSACOLA, Fla. ( WKRG ) — A woman has been sentenced after striking a cyclist and fleeing the scene of the crime, according to a release from the Office of State Attorney, First Judicial Circuit of Florida. According to the release, Christina Lynn Chenault, 40, hit a teenager on his bicycle at the Cross and Tarragona Streets intersection on Jan. 5, 2025, while driving with a suspended license. When officers responded, Chenault fled and did not pull over during the pursuit. While heading east on I-10, she was met with a blockade set up by the Florida Highway Patrol and made a U-turn. Officers performed a PIT maneuver and discovered the defendant had three young children in the car, the release said. She was sentenced to serve 15 years in state prison for Fleeing or Attempting to Elude a Law Enforcement Officer, three counts of Child Neglect, Leaving the Scene of a Crash with Injuries, Driving While License Suspended, and Reckless Driving. Her license was also revoked for the maximum penalty of five years. Chenault was serving her Okaloosa County probation sentence for 2023 charges of attempting to elude and drug charges at the time of the incident. She will be taken from Escambia County to Okaloosa County to resolve the pending violation. The Pensacola Police Department investigated the case while it was prosecuted by Assistant State Attorney Erin Ambrose. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WKRG News 5.
